extracted.intended_audience: CIA senior management, General Counsel, OPPB and legal/policy staff preparing an agency reply to OMB
extracted.subtask_description: Assess whether Executive Order 11671 / revised OMB Circular A-63 disclosure requirements apply to CIA participation in USIB and its subcommittees, and recommend the Agency's procedural response to OMB while preserving relations. Produce a draft reply and coordinate internal notification.

rubrics_metrics.name: Advisory committee definition / membership test
rubrics_metrics.description: USIB subcommittees would not be 'advisory committees' because they are composed wholly of government officials.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use the Executive Order's definitions (see subsections 1(6), (7) and (8)) to determine whether a body is an advisory committee. If membership is entirely government officials, treat it as not an 'advisory committee' for purposes of E.O. 11671/Circular A-63. Note that OMB's drafting intent may differ; explicitly cite the definitions when taking this position.

rubrics_metrics.name: Industry committee exclusion
rubrics_metrics.guidance: An 'industry committee' should consist of non-government (industry) participants. When asserting that a committee is not an industry committee, document the composition (government-only) and contrast with the Executive Order's industry committee definition.

rubrics_metrics.name: Interagency committee criterion
rubrics_metrics.description: USIB subcommittees are not 'interagency committees' because they are established by the Director of Central Intelligence, in his capacity as Chairman of USIB and under the authority of a National Security Council Intelligence Directive, and not 'by a department or agency.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: To classify a committee as an 'interagency committee' under the Order, it must be established by a department or agency. Where establishment is by the DCI under NSCID authority, argue non-applicability. Cite the specific EO language to support the interpretation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Legal conclusion on disclosure provisions' applicability
rubrics_metrics.description: The disclosure provisions of E.O. 11671 are inapplicable to CIA (the Agency should go on record with OMB in this regard).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: State the Agency's legal view clearly in the reply to OMB, but acknowledge uncertainty: 'While we believe this is the correct legal interpretation of the Order, it very well may be that OMB, in drafting the Order, did not mean to exclude the USIB committees.' Be prepared to address OMB's contrary intent or differing interpretation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consideration of prior practice and precedent
rubrics_metrics.description: The Agency has reported to OMB under the existing Circular A-63 and the then current Executive Order for the years 1966 through 1971 and the definitions of the two Orders are not significantly different in these regards.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When assessing applicability, account for historical reporting practice and precedent. Even if the legal interpretation supports non-applicability, past reporting to OMB may influence negotiations or expectations; document prior reports and the similarity/difference of definitions across Orders.

rubrics_metrics.name: Policy posture: cooperate while asserting authority
rubrics_metrics.description: Maintain very satisfactory relations with the International Division of OMB and be willing to furnish any information it desires concerning CIA participation in USIB and other committees, with or without the existence of an Executive Order requiring us to do so; at the same time make clear the Director's position and powers as head of Central Intelligence.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Adopt a dual posture in communications: (a) assure OMB of willingness to provide requested information to preserve good relations; (b) simultaneously state the Agency's legal position regarding non-applicability and the Director's authority. Use conciliatory language while firmly articulating legal basis.

rubrics_metrics.name: Recommended procedural actions for reply and coordination
rubrics_metrics.description: The draft reply at Tab B to the Assistant Director of OMB should be signed and dispatched; OPPB should advise the International Division of our reply to the Assistant Director and assure that Division that the Agency will furnish it whatever information on committee activities which the Division may request.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Follow the recommended internal routing: have the Executive Director sign the reply, dispatch promptly, and have OPPB notify and reassure OMB's International Division. Maintain internal distribution records (OGC, ExDir, ER, OPPB, OLC) and note concurrence (STATINTL) as appropriate.
